metadata.title: Infrastructure reliability incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output (not raw log lines or metric samples); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Reliability incident investigation of a production environment. Evidence consists of Elasticsearch aggregation results over application and proxy logs, Kubernetes, cloud-provider and host system events, Prometheus Alertmanager alerts, change-management / CI-CD audit records and metric anomaly detection. No root cause, impact or trigger is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Environment context: Organization: Merari Market (online retail); Platform: on-premises data center DC-B, server range 172.21.0.0/16; Kubernetes cluster merari-prod (kubeadm); Bare-metal Kubernetes workers; IPMI SEL and EDAC kernel messages are forwarded to Elasticsearch; data-center work uses DC- identifiers; Change management: production changes carry CHG- identifiers.
investigation_questions: Which host or node did the failure originate on? Give its hostname.
What is the IP address of the host or node where the failure originated?
Which memory module (DIMM slot) did the hardware event log identify?
Which Kubernetes node condition was reported for the failing node?
During what hour did the first signs of the failure appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.

What is the root cause category of the incident: configuration change, software defect, hardware failure, cloud provider failure, capacity exhaustion, automation error, certificate expiry, or third-party dependency failure?
Which of the three CIA components is primarily affected: availability, integrity, or confidentiality?
According to the error volume statistics, what single service emitted the most errors? Is it the root cause or a downstream symptom?
Which change restored normal service? Provide its change identifier.
